newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SE Asian buyers test prices for August soymeal.
newsitem.headline: SE Asian buyers test prices for August soymeal.

text.p: The Southeast Asian oilseeds market perked up on Thursday as inquiries flooded in from potential buyers for August cargoes of soymeal after Chicago futures prices fell sharply overnight, dealers said.
"There were a lot of inquiries for meal. Everybody is testing the waters," a dealer for a U.S. commodity house said.
"They're looking at soymeal prices in Chicago and monitoring Project A. This level is pretty interesting for some chaps," an analyst for a trading company in Singapore added.
The July soymeal contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) finished limit down on Wednesday, diving US$10 to end at $273.10 a ton.
The July contract slipped further in the CBOT's Project A after-hours trading system in Asia, shedding one dollar to $272.10 a ton at 0800 GMT.
"With the market coming down, people are taking a real close look at prices," a trader said. "I wouldn't be surprised if something had been done although we have not heard of anything yet."
"There have been a lot of inquiries, but everybody is just checking the price for now," a U.S. dealer said.

Traders estimate that buyers in Indonesia will be in the market for about 50,000 tonnes of soymeal for August shipment. Thailand may also be looking for around 40,000 tonnes while Malaysia was said to be open for about 20,000 tonnes.
The likely origin of the soymeal would be either Brazil or Argentina, but not the United States.
"U.S. meal is too expensive for buyers here," a dealer said.
Another dealer said U.S. soymeal is "completely irrelevant" and said meal from Brazil or Argentina fetched quotes at a substantial discount.

U.S. meal coming into Southeast Asia was quoted by the trade at around $325-$330 a tonne C&F for July/August shipment on a Panamax. Brazilian or Argentine meal, on the other hand, was quoted at around $300-$302 a tonne C&F on the same basis.
Dealers said they were also waiting for a possible soymeal purchase by Philippine feed mills which may reach about 15,000 to 20,000 tonnes for July/August shipment.
"They should be buying soon, especially with prices coming off so sharply," a dealer said.
The corn market in the region was subdued with most buyers adequately covered for their nearby requirements, dealers said.
"Business is next-to-nothing," one said.
Corn-buying by Thailand has eased sharply after buyers from that country bought the 200,000 tonnes allowed under a tariff-free scheme.
"I think that's been all bought," a trader said, adding though that some buyers there may still eventually buy up to 50,000 tonnes corn for far forward delivery.

Chinese and Argentine corn was still being quoted at about $134-$136 a tonne C&F for July/August shipment and at a slight discount to U.S. origin, but there were very few takers in the market, dealers said.
"There's very little going on in corn," a dealer said. "It may stay that way for a while."
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
